messages:
maya: Heads-up — enterprise customer asked for 3-tier audit export SLAs (realtime, 24h, 7d) + explicit BYO-key exceptions for archived evidence. They're pushing SOC2 evidence packaging as part of contract. Need acceptance criteria and a fallback path if BYOK handshake fails.

sam: Thanks. Do we have precedent for 3-tier SLA? I know we offer archive retrieval within 48h today.

jon: We don't have realtime export currently. Closest is streaming webhook for events but not full evidence bundles. Realtime would need synchronous packaging + signed manifest.

irene: Packaging for SOC2 typically means signed proof-of-delivery + tamper-evident checksum (sha256). We can produce a tarball with manifest.json and sig using customer's public key.

maya: Good. For contract we should define: 1) SLA tiers (RT <5min, 24h, 7d), 2) BYOK handshake: handshake window & fallback, 3) Evidence format + signature scheme, 4) Retention/TTL options per tier.

sam: On BYOK handshake: proposal = attempt handshake for 72h, if fails we route to escrow flow (customer notified, evidence stored encrypted with Redwood KMS but flagged for re-encryption later). Need clear contractual language on escrow risk.

jon: Ops concerns: Escrow flows increase complexity for key rotation and for support. We should include an "escape hatch" where customer can request manual retrieval (SLA: 7d) while key issue is resolved. Also add quota guardrails to prevent wide blast during realtime requests.

irene: Implementation notes:
```
- export pipeline: assemble events -> normalize -> package -> sign -> upload to customer-specified S3/URL
- if BYOK present: encrypt package with customer key before upload; verify sig on upload
- fallback: encrypt with Redwood KMS, attach escrow flag + re-encrypt-on-churn job
```

maya: Nice. For acceptance criteria I propose short list we can commit to in contract:
- Evidence bundle format (manifest + sha256 + signer identity)
- SLA definitions per tier (p99 delivery latency)
- BYOK handshake window & escrow default behaviour documented
- Operational runbook: who to contact, playbook for re-encryption, and audit trail visible in Console

sam: Add security gating: KMS attestation proof (HSM-backed) for Redwood escrow, and optional customer-requested HSM attestation copy. Also require automated regression eval on integrity checks for every release affecting export pipeline.

jon: We should prototype with 24h tier first. Low blast, catches most cases. If that works, add realtime as premium (requires infra + perf testing).

maya: Agreed. Action items:
- irene: draft spec for evidence format + handshake states (ETA: Wed)
- sam: draft security language for contract + escrow risks (ETA: Thu)
- jon: capacity sketch for realtime tier and quota defaults (ETA: Fri)
- maya: collect customer sample contracts and draft SLA table (ETA: Fri)

irene: I'll include sample manifest schema and example signed bundle in the doc. Will put a sample curl to upload:
```
curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" --data-binary @evidence.tar.gz "https://customer-s3.example.com/path/evidence.tar.gz"
```

deploy-bot: New doc created: https://notion.redwood/product/audit-export-byo-proposal (created by maya)

maya: Thanks. One more ask from legal: define retention implications if customer requests deletion during escrow window. We need a deterministic policy (delete on receipt of customer key OR provide proof of deletion with attestation).

sam: Policy idea: If customer requests deletion but BYOK missing, we can mark object for deletion and provide signed proof-of-deletion of Redwood-held copy. If later the customer supplies key and requests re-encrypt+deliver, we treat as new request and log it. Need legal check.

jon: I'll add supportability notes: ops will open a ticket template and SLA clock starts on successful key handshake or escrow flag creation — whichever occurs first.

maya: Perfect. Let's sync tomorrow 10a to review irene's spec and close contract language. :calendar: :thumbsup:
